headline: Highest risk is compliance/data leakage if Authelia’s broad egress feeds Mem0 memory flows; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are otherwise limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, while Mem0 shows no I/O surfaces or egress. Without a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects Authelia outputs into Mem0 prompts or memory writes, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or message queue is introduced, treat content as untrusted.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe Authelia logs or responses into Mem0 as instructions.
Add explicit provenance labels before any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer/allowlist for any shared text channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can handle OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic; Mem0 is a memory system with no documented egress. If sensitive identity or session data reaches Mem0, the pair can retain or expose it through downstream memory workflows. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Authelia-authenticated identity data is written into Mem0 memory entries, leakage risk exists.
IF either agent is configured to store request/response payloads, sensitive fields may persist beyond the original session.
mitigations: Avoid sending tokens, headers, or claims into Mem0.
Redact identity attributes before any handoff.
Disable verbose request logging on Authelia.
Review Mem0 retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: add field-level filtering between the systems.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls, while Mem0 has no documented network egress and no write surfaces are listed. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, shared filesystem writes, or locking conflicts, so only a small conflict risk remains if an external orchestrator later gives both access to the same resource.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same external store, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared OAuth scopes or shared database credentials, re-evaluate for write contention.
mitigations: Keep credentials separate.
Do not share mutable databases between the agents.
Use per-agent service accounts.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions through OIDC/ForwardAuth, and Mem0 is a memory/knowledge component that may preserve or reuse upstream outputs. If Mem0 treats Authelia-derived text as authoritative, errors can cascade into later retrieval or agent behavior. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Mem0 stores Authelia outputs without validation, downstream errors can propagate.
IF another agent consumes Mem0 memory as ground truth, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Mark Authelia outputs as untrusted metadata.
Require validation before writing to Mem0.
Store source references alongside memory entries.
Limit Mem0 writes to non-authoritative notes.
requires-engineering: add a verification gate before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are explicitly listed for either agent, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. Authelia’s broad egress could move regulated identity data, but there is no documented residency or certification mismatch with Mem0. Because the compliance pathway is plausible but unproven, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is routed from Authelia into Mem0, review residency and retention obligations.
IF Mem0 is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules, align policies before use.
mitigations: Classify any identity data before transfer.
Confirm retention settings in both systems.
Document the data flow for audits.
Restrict Mem0 to non-regulated fields.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
